title: Transfer item ownership
lede: A serialized item now moves into the actual owner’s checkout. The checkout requester remains the shared source for personal gear, accountability, reminders, overdue handling, and returns.

stats.n: The camera leaves; pooled batteries remain. Verified by browser assertions.
Existing item and active allocation move in one serializable transaction.

sections.heading: The camera leaves the old checkout
sections.note: Same deterministic shared checkout, recipient, action, and desktop viewport. Baseline is the pre-change working-tree implementation saved alongside this review; it was uncommitted at task start. The API responses are fixtures, so this proves client rendering, not a live database transfer.

pairs.title: After assigning or transferring CAM-104
pairs.sub: The previous implementation left the camera inline under the shared checkout; the new implementation removes it from that checkout.
pairs.beforeCap: 2 rows: camera with an inline holder label, plus pooled batteries.
pairs.afterCap: 1 row: pooled batteries. CAM-104 is on the receiving owner’s checkout.

sections.heading: The confirmation names the ownership change
sections.note: Same shared checkout and 390px viewport before choosing a recipient. Both dialogs were opened by the same repeatable Playwright test.

pairs.title: Narrow-screen transfer dialog
pairs.beforeCap: The old dialog explicitly promised that the item would stay on this checkout.
pairs.afterCap: The new dialog explains receiving-checkout reuse or creation, the unchanged deadline, and preserved scan history.

changes.was: Only assignedUserId changed; the original checkout still owned gear and downstream actions.
changes.now: The original item and active allocation move to a compatible personal checkout, or one created with the original context. Legacy assignee metadata is cleared.

changes.was: Inline assignment did not change the custody ledger.
changes.now: Original scans, photos, allocation IDs/dates, and source reservation remain intact. Both checkouts receive audit entries linking the item, allocation, original evidence, recipient, and reason.

changes.was: The old checkout remained the source for return work.
changes.now: A checkout with no remaining actual custody is retained as a cancelled transfer, without a fabricated return or return badge. Receiving-owner reminders are scheduled after commit.

verification: 64 focused Vitest tests pass across transfer, stale/retry/integrity guards, accountability, reminders, kiosk returns and mutation freshness. Database calls are mocked; this is not PostgreSQL rollback or concurrent-session runtime proof.
Authenticated Playwright: 4 transfer cases plus sign-in pass; the baseline run also passes. Booking and mutation responses use deterministic isolated fixtures, without live gear changes.
TypeScript, ESLint, app-only production build, docs/codemaps, migration-prefix check and git diff --check pass. No database migration is required.

Initial browser launch was blocked by the macOS sandbox; approved execution outside that sandbox resolved it. A cold server compile exceeded the default 30-second sign-in timeout; the warm run with a 120-second budget passed.
notes: Local source and local review only. Nothing committed, pushed, deployed, or corrected in production.
A real database transfer/read-back, real recipient notification delivery, and physical kiosk return still need rollout acceptance.
Original evidence stays attached to its historical checkout; audit entries on both sides link the transfer. Pooled bulk gear is not distributed among recipients.
